traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and named requirements for docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are implemented and verified.
The valid-annotation-format rule supports both nested (story.pattern/req.pattern, story.example/req.example) and flat (storyPathPattern/storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern/requirementIdExample) configuration shapes. Patterns are validated by attempting to construct RegExp objects; invalid patterns generate configuration diagnostics (invalidRuleConfiguration) while the rule falls back to default patterns, preserving backward-compatible behavior. Example strings are correctly incorporated into error messages, with nested examples taking precedence over flat examples.
JSON Schema for the rule options includes all new fields and is used by ESLint; configuration tests confirm schema properties and rejection of unknown options. The main rule uses the shared option resolver and reports any configuration errors before processing comments, as required.
User-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md describes these options, defaults, precedence rules, and behavior in detail, and shows how they complement the existing valid-story-reference configuration.
All tests that exercise these behaviors and explicitly reference this story (and its requirement IDs) pass in the current Jest run. Therefore, this story is fully implemented according to its specification.
